title: CUDA + driver sensitivity experiments across cloud GPU SKUs
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note for a focused set of sensitivity experiments: how CUDA toolkit and NVIDIA driver versions interact with cloud SKUs (A100-, H100-, L40S-class instances) to change microkernel behavior, tail latency, and end-to-end batch throughput for our serving runtime. Goal is to identify safe driver/toolkit combinations we can recommend for Hosted and Dedicated, and highlight fragilities we should guard with runtime fallbacks.

Quick summary / TL;DR: (high-level findings)
- Small-sequence single-request latency is most sensitive to driver + cublas/cuBLASLt versions on A100 SKUs; on our L40S tests it was less variable but showed higher jitter when CUDA 12.1 + driver 535.* was used.
- H100 shows consistent throughput advantage at high batch sizes, but driver mismatches (CUDA 12.x versus 11.8 stacks) caused unexpected kernel fallback into slower GEMM paths for quantized models (q4* kernels), reducing throughput by ~15–30% in some runs.
- nsight system traces revealed kernel launch serialization on nodes with older drivers (CN driver 470/495 era) when we enabled multi-stream concurrent dispatch; upgrading to 525+ eliminated the serialization.
- We observed a reproducible 6–12% throughput delta between two nominally identical cloud SKUs (same GPU type) from different providers under identical driver/CUDA stacks; likely due to PCIe topology and host CPU scheduling differences.

Why this matters for Redwood:
- Customers expect predictable latency SLOs across Dedicated and Private. If driver/CUDA combos can change infer-time kernel choices, we must pin validated stacks or add runtime detection/fallbacks.
- For Hosted (multi-tenant), we need a matrix of safe stacks per region/SKU.

Experimental matrix (short):
- GPUs: NVIDIA A100 40GB (GCP a2/highgpu-ish SKUs), H100 (various cloud SKUs), L40S (NVIDIA L40S as offered by partner clouds).
- Cloud providers: GCP, AWS, Azure (picked representative SKUs where available).
- Driver versions tested: 470.141.03, 495.44, 510.60, 525.60, 535.86 (representative).
- CUDA toolkits: 11.8, 12.0, 12.1 (we had prebuilt containers for 11.8 and 12.1).
- Model workloads: small decoder-only (7B), medium (13B), large 70B-ish (64k params not used here) with two precisions: fp16 and int8/q4 quantized path used by our runtime.
- Workload patterns: single-request seq=32, batch=1; burst 8x concurrent reqs; steady throughput batch=8, seq=1024; long-seq tail tests seq=8192.
- Tools: nsys (system profile), ncu (kernel profiling), dstat + perf for host CPU/jitter, logged runtime traces.

Representative commands (what we ran):
- nsys trace: nsys profile --output trace_a100_driver525 --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt,syscalls python -m scripts.run_rps --model llama-13b --precision fp16 --batch 8 --seq 1024
- ncu kernels: ncu --kernel-regex "gemm|attention|multihead" --target-processes all -o ncu_a100_525 report
- Runtime invocation (our runner): PYTHONPATH=. CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -m redwood.serving.bench --config configs/rps_a100.yaml --cuda-toolkit 11.8

Notable micro-observations: (detailed)
1) cublasLt kernel selection flip: On A100 with CUDA 12.1 + driver 535.*, when running q4 quantized matmuls we saw the runtime pick a different cuBLAS Lt heuristic causing 20–30% lower throughput for the attention GEMM. Trace point: many more small-GEMM launches vs a batched large-GEMM path used on 11.8 stacks. Reproduced 3x.
2) H100 and Tensor-Engine enabled stacks: some tensor core optimized kernels only kick in for CUDA 12+ and specific driver combos. On H100 SKUs with driver 510 and CUDA 11.8 container we saw lower throughput vs driver 525 + CUDA12. Upgrading improved throughput by ~18% for fp16 batched decode.
3) Host CPU binding / cgroup interplay: on Azure L40S SKUs we saw occasional spikes in latency correlated with host CPU stealing for iommu tasks. These spikes were amplified on older drivers that used CPU-side decompression / plugin callbacks.
4) PCIe vs NVLink impact: Multi-GPU sharded KV cache benchmarks were sensitive to PCIe topologies; H100 nodes with NVLink (DGX-like) retained predictable latency even with older drivers. Cloud SKUs that had a PCIe-only topology showed more variability under high mem-copy pressure.

Concrete reproducible case (notes to engineering):
- On GCP A100 instance n1-a100-40gb-v2, with container image built from CUDA 12.1 + driver 535 base we observed the q4 GEMM path regression. Rebuild the runtime linked against cublasLt 12.1 and test with the following steps: 1) run nsys trace during warmup (first 10k tokens), 2) capture cuBLAS Lt heuristic call logs, 3) force the fallback to our old GEMM (via env override REDWOOD_FORCE_GEMM=v1) to confirm throughput delta.

Data excerpts (representative numbers, average of 3 runs):
- 13B fp16, batch=8, seq=1024: A100 (CUDA11.8/driver525): 420 tokens/s; A100 (CUDA12.1/driver535): 340 tokens/s (–19%).
- 7B q4, batch=1, seq=32: H100 (CUDA12.1/driver525): 320 tokens/s; H100 (CUDA11.8/driver510): 257 tokens/s (+19% with newer driver).
- L40S, fp16, batch=8: stable throughput similar to H100 at long seqs, but jitter (P99 latency) spiked from 110ms to 185ms under driver 535; lower drivers had lower P99 but worse median.
(These are representative numbers for triage; will expand with full CSVs in the artifact link.)

Anomalies & hypotheses:
- Hypothesis 1: CUDA 12.x + new drivers update heuristic thresholds in cuBLAS Lt that change kernel choices for small/mid-size GEMMs used in quantized attention; this leads to worse caching/tiling for our workloads.
- Hypothesis 2: Some cloud images ship with mismatched kernel modules or older NVML/ucore; userland driver vs kernel mismatch can cause intermittent synchronization stalls.
- Hypothesis 3: Host BIOS/firmware differences (PCIE ASPM settings) lead to observed throughput deltas even with same driver. Cloud provider variability plays a role.

Next steps / checklist:
- [ ] Expand runs to 5 providers and gather full CSVs for all combinations (scripts already in experiments/driver_sensitivity).
- [ ] Add a focused test that pins cuBLASLt heuristics (if available) and measure differences to isolate heuristic flips.
- [ ] Build a short doc with validated driver/CUDA matrix that we can pin for Dedicated contracts (recommendations + known risk combos).
- [ ] Add runtime detection (on startup) to capture cuBLAS driver/toolkit versions and log a compatibility score.
- [ ] Run long-duration stability runs (48h) for the candidate stacks to catch slower memory-leak-type regressions.

Action items (who/when):
- Diego: run the expanded 5-provider matrix, collect traces, update CSVs by 2025-02-14.
- Priya: prototype runtime startup detection and env var override for GEMM selection (REDWOOD_FORCE_GEMM) by 2025-02-10.
- Ava: synthesize a 1-page decision matrix for product (Hosted vs Dedicated) by 2025-02-20.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally a working doc; raw traces live in gs://redwood-bench/traces/driver-sensitivity/ (link in PR).
- If you rerun experiments, please include nsys traces and attach the .qdrep to the artifacts folder.

Appendix (short reproducibility commands & env):
- Container base: nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:22.12-py3 (CUDA11.8) and nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:23.11-py3 (CUDA12.1)
- nsys: 2023.3; ncu: 2024.1
- env overrides we used: REDWOOD_FORCE_GEMM= (empty|v1|v2), CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=0, CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8
- Example runner (one-liner): docker run --gpus all --rm -v $PWD:/workspace -w /workspace --entrypoint /bin/bash nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:23.11-py3 -c "source venv/bin/activate && nsys profile --output tmp && PYTHONPATH=. CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -m redwood.serving.bench --model llama-13b --precision fp16 --batch 8 --seq 1024"

Raw trace pointers (short):
- gs://redwood-bench/traces/driver-sensitivity/a100_cuda11.8_driver525_q4_20250109.qdrep
- gs://redwood-bench/traces/driver-sensitivity/a100_cuda12.1_driver535_q4_20250110.qdrep

Open questions we should answer before final recommendations:
- Are we comfortable recommending CUDA 12.1 stacks for Dedicated customers who need q4 paths, or should we hold to 11.8 until cuBLASLt heuristics are better understood?
- Can we add an automated boot-time compatibility probe that runs a micro-GEMM sample to detect pathological kernel choices and auto-fallback?

If you have other angles to test (e.g., kernel module versions, different distro kernels, or microcode/BIOS settings), add to the checklist and tag me.

-- Ava
